scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Sekete originates from the Saramaka Maroon community in Suriname, descendants of enslaved Africans who escaped plantations and formed independent tribes in the rainforest.
The dance is linked to the Winti religion, which incorporates West African spiritual elements and has evolved with Christian and indigenous influences.
Sekete is one of the original Winti dances, reflecting the cultural and spiritual life of the Maroons since the colonial era.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Sekete is performed during social gatherings and spiritual ceremonies within the Saramaka Maroon community.
It is connected to the Winti religion, embodying spirits and ancestral reverence.
The dance serves both entertainment and ritual purposes, reflecting the community's cultural identity and spiritual beliefs.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music accompanying Sekete features apinti drums, traditional Maroon drums with a deep, resonant sound.
Dancers wear kwakwa ankle rattles that add a percussive layer synchronized with the drum rhythms.
Listen for the apinti drums, kwakwa ankle rattles.
The music features deep, resonant apinti drum beats layered with sharp, rhythmic shaking of ankle rattles, creating a textured percussive soundscape that guides the dancers' movements.
